newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Secret Beijing visit boosts HK Catholic confidence.
newsitem.headline: Secret Beijing visit boosts HK Catholic confidence.

text.p: Catholic Church leaders from Hong Kong made an undisclosed visit to China to discuss the territory's handover in a month and returned more confident about the future, church authorities said on Sunday. Three of the top Chinese clerics here explored the outlook for religion when Hong Kong ceases to be a British colony and joins China as a mainly-autonomous region from July 1.
Their two-day Beijing visit from May 20 apparently indicated approval of the Vatican which has had sometimes-stormy relations with the officially atheist and communist rulers of modern China.

Details were disclosed in a front-page report in the official church paper here, Sunday Examiner which quoted the delegation leader as saying that frank and friendly talks had "strengthened our confidence."
China has promised to respect religion, among other aspects of Hong Kong's way of life, for 50 years but some leaders of various faiths have expressed unease about civil liberties in the future.
Hong Kong has about 250,000 Catholics in a population of 6.4 million, nearly all Chinese.
The Sunday Examiner said Catholic leaders met Beijing Religious Affairs officials and members of the government.
In a trip without media coverage, Bishop Joseph Zen, Bishop John Tong and Vicar-general Father Dominic Chan spent two days with state officials and religious representatives in the Chinese capital.
They went on an official invitation from the Religious Affairs Bureau of the ruling State Council after church leaders, backed by Cardinal John Baptist Wu, made inquiries about a visit to China.
Thanking the Chinese for hospitality, Bishop Zen said: "We highly appreciate the leaders' open attitude towards us....As there was no media coverage, we were able to express our opinions freely.
"The meeting has strengthened our confidence and we hope that in future, from time to time, we will be able to exchange views with Beijing leaders."
The delegation was determined to help the Hong Kong Catholic church grow and hoped to have a closer relationship with the church on the mainland.

The Beijing government does not recognise the ultimate authority of the Vatican in religious affairs and insists that Chinese Catholics worshipping openly do so under the auspices of the state-sponsored Catholic Patriotic Association.
